manifest.device_read_resolution: every device read is resolved by the stub: $2002 from the dot counter, $4016 from the scripted pad, everything else 0. In T each such read is an unconstrained byte, so this run fixes one choice out of 256 per read; the reads the run actually made are listed per variant.
manifest.tracer: formal.dyn.tracer with the device stub it documents

model_variant: T, formal/model/transitions.py without MA-NMI-EDGE and without MA-NMI-LATENCY
not_a_hardware_claim: An NMI is taken here at an instruction boundary chosen by the experiment, not by a vertical blank.  No NES can deliver two NMI entries without a new vblank between them, so nothing in this report says anything about what a console does.  It is a concrete witness for the model variant T, which admits these boundaries, and therefore evidence that the two timing assumptions are load-bearing rather than cosmetic.

what_the_witness_shows: In T, from a state the image reaches in ordinary play, the program counter can be made to leave $8000-$FFFF entirely, which refutes the fetch-from-ROM property for that variant. It says nothing about T_V2, in which the behaviour is excluded by assumption, and nothing about hardware.
